§9.5.1 Blank and Spacer Rows

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-blank-and-spacer-rows · tables either rows disputed

⚖️ Equivalent forms

A genuinely printed blank row inside a table MAY be rendered as an empty row or left out; both forms conform, and a document MUST use one of them throughout. A blank row that is the only thing separating two groups of rows SHOULD be rendered as an empty row.

| ROU assets total   | 10,234 |
|                    |        |   ← printed blank row: on this page it is the
| Lease liabilities: |        |     only section boundary — rendered as an empty row

When the blank row is load-bearing

On a page with no rules, no bands and no repeated headers, the whitespace is the structure. Dropping a blank row there merges two sections the page deliberately kept apart — as in a lease note where a single blank line is all that separates the right-of-use totals from "Lease liabilities:".

  • A blank row whose removal would change how a reader groups the rows around it SHOULD be rendered as a row of empty cells, in its printed position.
  • A purely decorative blank line — even spacing between every row, padding at the foot of a block — carries no such meaning and MAY be left out.
  • An empty row MUST NOT be rendered where the page prints none: the row is kept because it is printed, never added to make groups easier to read.

✅ Sample — ert

A genuinely printed blank row separates the 00xx class codes from the 01xx codes, in every block; it is kept as a row of empty cells. The four side-by-side CLASS CODE | ELR | D RATIO blocks continue one class-code series, so each block is its own table (see Column Continuation§9.2.2); the first is shown.

Encoding an empty region

The encoding of an empty region is free. Its existence is not.

  • An empty region inside a table body MAY be encoded as individual empty <td> cells or as one blank cell spanning it (colspan / rowspan): three leading empty <td>s per row and one colspan="3" rowspan="8" blank block render identically, and both conform. Where the page draws no separation inside the empty region, neither encoding is preferred.
  • Carve-out: in a loss triangle or similar matrix, every empty position MUST be its own empty cell, never part of a span — each is a distinct, meaningful absence. See Triangles and Matrix Tables§9.8.2.
  • The half that is not free: the cells and columns MUST exist. A column proven only by its header still exists (Barely-Existing Columns and Headers§9.3.1), and every value in it MUST stay reachable. Encoding is a choice; deletion is an error.
  • Blank space beside a header label is not free: it MUST be rendered as separate empty cells, not as an extended span, unless the page prints a genuinely merged cell. See Barely-Existing Columns and Headers§9.3.1.
